# `liber:modem@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:modem` package (`modem.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem modems - SIM, registration and the one data context this system supports, over four separately granted authorities.  FOUR AUTHORITIES, NOT ONE. OBSERVING a modem (`modem`) names no subscriber and changes nothing. USING it for data (`modem-data`) activates and deactivates the context a policy allows, and nothing else. Its SUBSCRIBER IDENTITY (`modem-identity`) and its MANAGEMENT - PIN, PUK (`modem-manage`) - are authorities of their own, denied by default. Every connection but the first is minted by PermissionManager through the private `modem-admin`, for one component, one modem and one SIM, and lives only as long as that component does.  NETWORKSERVICE OWNS IP. A context this service activates is installed as NetworkService's uplink through a private link-admin endpoint; addresses, routes, DNS and traffic are NetworkService's, and no client of this service is ever handed a packet channel or a network administration handle.

## Interfaces

### interface `modem`

OBSERVATION: every modem, its limits, and a watch that coalesces to the newest snapshot.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `modems` | `modems() -> result<list<modem-status>, error>` |  |
| 2 | `limits` | `limits() -> result<modem-limits, error>` |  |
| 3 | `watch` | `watch() -> result<stream<modem-watch>, error>` |  |

### interface `modem-data`

DATA: the context the grant's policy allows, on the modem and SIM it was granted for.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `activate` | `activate(modem: modem-id) -> result<context-status, error>` |  |
| 2 | `deactivate` | `deactivate(context: context-id) -> result<unit, error>` |  |
| 3 | `status` | `status() -> result<modem-status, error>` |  |

### interface `modem-identity`

THE SUBSCRIBER'S IDENTITY, and nothing else.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `identity` | `identity(modem: modem-id) -> result<identity, error>` |  |

### interface `modem-manage`

MANAGEMENT: the counters, and PIN and PUK entry - one attempt per call, never replayed. A PIN reaches the modem and nowhere else: no log, no state record and no reply carries it.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `attempts` | `attempts(modem: modem-id) -> result<attempts, error>` |  |
| 2 | `enter-pin` | `enter-pin(modem: modem-id, pin: string, acknowledge-unknown: bool) -> result<sim-pin-outcome, error>` |  |
| 3 | `enter-puk` | `enter-puk(modem: modem-id, puk: string, new-pin: string, acknowledge-unknown: bool) -> result<sim-pin-outcome, error>` |  |

### interface `modem-admin`

THE MINTING ENDPOINT, PermissionManager's alone. The alias names a modem the service's configuration binds to provider metadata, and resolves to exactly one current publication or the mint fails. The connection is bound to the modem and SIM current at minting, and lives as long as `owner` does.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `mint` | `mint(kind: grant-kind, alias: string, policy: data-policy, owner: handle<task>) -> result<modem-grant, error>` |  |
